doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Herb Alpert's re-formed Tijuana Brass
summary: He played in Alpert's jazz-oriented Tijuana Brass revival in the mid-70s; it never caught on but was first class fun.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see you even did some work with the Tijuana Brass?

I was with Herb Alpert’s re-formed, he re-invented the Tijuana Brass ten years after the big hit. It was the middle 70s and he wanted to come back with a more jazz oriented — he wanted like a Chuck Mangione type approach, kind of a picturesque, macho, flashy jazz approach with a lot of rhythm and a lot of Latin. And it was fun. That was a hot band, very good musicians on it including some from the original Tijuana Brass like the drummer, Nick Ceroli and John Pisano the guitar player. It was a hot band. But it never caught on with the public the way the original band did. But we had a ball. We traveled around for a couple of years and it was like being with the New York Yankees, it was first class. It was really fun.
